key_insight: Targeting fine-grained image details and enforcing coherent patch-level alignment mitigates the high-variance, nearly-orthogonal gradients caused by crop-based transfer attacks (e.g., M-Attack), producing more stable and effective black-box attacks on LVLMs.
problem_solved: Stabilizes and improves transfer-based black-box adversarial attacks on Large Vision–Language Models by addressing missing gradients, ViT translation sensitivity, and the high-variance gradients induced by local crop-level matching.
method: Analyze failure mode: show crop-level local matching yields high-variance, near-orthogonal gradient directions across iterations, exacerbated by ViT translation sensitivity.
Fine-grained detail targeting: align and optimize at patch/texture level instead of coarse crops to preserve coherent local correspondence between source and target.
Optimization stabilization: aggregate cross-crop consistency and gradient-smoothing/aggregation so updates point in consistent directions and improve transferability with limited queries.
impact: Provides a more reliable way to evaluate and perform black-box attacks on LVLMs, improving transferability and query efficiency; the insights also guide defenses and robustness testing for multimodal models.
visual_elements: Schematic comparing M-Attack (crop-level matching) vs Fine-Grained Detail Targeting (patch-level alignment)

paper_title: Pushing the Frontier of Black-Box LVLM Attacks via Fine-Grained Detail Targeting
paper_authors: Xiaohan Zhao, Zhaoyi Li, Yaxin Luo, Jiacheng Cui, Zhiqiang Shen
